tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear Path for Target Disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To move a disk that is not on top, you must first relocate every smaller disk that sits above it to another peg, making the target disk the topmost piece.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to move a disk that has one or more smaller disks stacked above it on its current peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: If disk 4 is under disks 2 and 3 on peg A, first move disks 2 and 3 elsewhere, then move disk 4.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Build Goal Stack in Decreasing Size
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Construct the final tower on the goal peg by placing disks from the largest down to the smallest, ensuring each placed disk is larger than any disk that will be placed later.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When assembling the final configuration on the target peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: After placing disk 5 on the goal peg, place disk 4, then 3, then 2, then 1.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive Phase Planning (Move‑k‑Disks)
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Solve a sub‑problem of moving k disks by recursively moving the top k‑1 disks to an auxiliary peg, moving the kth (largest) disk to the destination, then moving the k‑1 disks onto it.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to transfer a stack of multiple disks between pegs.
tower-of-hanoi.example: To move disks 1‑3 from peg A to peg B, first move disks 1‑2 to peg C, then move disk 3 to B, then move disks 1‑2 onto disk 3.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Do Not Prematurely Place Small Disks on Goal
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Never move a small disk onto the goal peg before all larger disks that must sit below it have already been placed there, to avoid blocking larger disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When deciding whether to move a small disk to the goal peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Do not place disk 1 on the goal peg while disks 5, 4, 3, 2 are still missing.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Legal Move Invariant
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Every move must satisfy two conditions: the source disk is the topmost disk on its peg, and the destination peg’s top disk (if any) is larger than the moving disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: You cannot move disk 4 onto a peg whose top disk is 2.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Treat Existing Goal Disks as Fixed Base
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Once a disk is correctly placed on the goal peg and all larger disks beneath it are also correctly placed, treat that disk as immovable and do not disturb it while completing the rest of the tower.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After a disk has reached its final position on the goal peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: After placing disk 5 at the bottom of the goal peg, never move it again.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Exploit the Smallest Disk’s Flexibility
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The smallest disk can be placed on any peg without violating size constraints, making it an ideal temporary buffer for rearranging other disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need a free peg or to clear a path for larger disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Move disk 1 to an empty peg to free up the peg holding disk 3.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Post‑Construction Verification
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After generating the complete move list, replay the moves from the initial configuration to verify that each move is legal and that the final configuration matches the goal.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After you have produced a move sequence, before submitting it.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Simulate the moves step‑by‑step and check that the final peg arrangement equals the goal.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Recognize Classic Single‑Peg Configuration
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Detect when all disks start stacked on a single peg and the goal is the same ordered stack on another peg; in this case, the standard optimal Hanoi solution applies.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the initial state has all disks on one peg and the goal is to move them to a different peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: All disks on peg 0, goal is all disks on peg 2.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Generate Moves Recursively with Explicit Disk IDs
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Use a recursive function that, for k disks, first generates the move sequence for k‑1 disks, then moves the kth disk, then generates the sequence for k‑1 disks again, while explicitly recording each move as [disk_id, from_peg, to_peg].
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When implementing an algorithmic solution to produce the move list.
tower-of-hanoi.example: For k=3, the generated moves are: move 1, move 2, move 1, move 3, move 1, move 2, move 1.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Violating size rule: moving a larger disk onto a smaller one.
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may focus on moving a desired disk without checking the size of the top disk on the destination peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always compare the moving disk’s size with the destination peg’s top disk; only move if the destination is empty or its top disk is larger.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a non‑top disk without clearing the path.
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may try to move a target disk that is buried under smaller disks, overlooking the need to free it first.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Apply the Clear Path for Target Disk principle: relocate all smaller disks above the target before moving it.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Final configuration does not match the goal state.
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may stop generating moves prematurely or misplace a disk, leading to an incorrect final arrangement.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: After generating the move list, run Post‑Construction Verification to ensure the final state equals the goal.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Incorrect peg indexing (off‑by‑one or swapped pegs).
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: Confusion between 0‑based indexing used by the verifier and natural 1‑based counting.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always label pegs as 0, 1, 2 and double‑check each move’s from‑peg and to‑peg indices.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Premature placement of small disks on the goal.
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may move a small disk to the goal peg before larger disks that belong below it have been placed.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Apply the Do Not Prematurely Place Small Disks on Goal principle; only move a small disk onto the goal after all larger required disks are already there.
